findings.text: follow-on: both arms of the recorded baseline_suite/after_suite pair name only tests/test_dispatch_launch_is_not_its_own_conflict.py, while the node's actual gate (its `tests` field) runs four files including the new test file; the derived added-failure count still reads 0 either way (the new file is added, not failing at base, and the four-file head gate shows the same two pre-existing failures), but a reader of the recorded pair alone cannot see the new file's passing arm.

follow-on: `_peer_claim_is_a_later_racing_arrival` orders two racing claims by `registered_at`, which is `_utc_now()` — host-local wall clock at second precision — so two dispatches issued from different hosts whose clocks differ could rank the later-registered claim as earlier and leave the earlier one to refuse; tie-break by run id only settles equal timestamps, not skewed ones. Dispatches usually originate from one coordinator host, so the exposure is low, but a monotonic or cross-host-comparable registration token would remove it.

follow-on: two cases in this file remain red at head (2 failed, 29 passed) because the refusal message they assert now names a derived landing fragment (docs/evidence/fragments/fixture/node-other.html) where the test asserts the declared path src/claimed.py; the node recorded them as pre-existing (reproduced with the unmodified dispatch.py at base, base-existing-conflicts.log) and they sit outside this node's write scope, so they are a standing follow-on rather than this node's defect.

justifications.durability: the guards are real and independent — the negative control (an order-blind claim check that refuses any overlapping binding claim) reddens the race case so the earlier dispatch no longer survives, and the ordering case reddens on the same mutation — and the tests assert the ordering against its worst inputs (equal registration times fall to the run id, a launched claim refuses, an unorderable claim refuses, a dispatch holding no claim refuses). Gaps: the ordering compares host-local wall-clock `created_at` at second precision, so two dispatches from different hosts whose clocks differ could mis-order and the wrong one could withdraw (recorded as a follow-on); and if the registered-first dispatch later fails for an unrelated reason the paths are left with no worker, which the fix does not address (inherent to first-wins).
justifications.evidence: the evidence is genuine and falsifiable: I re-ran the node's own gate on the reviewed worktree at 4dc8ff94 (`pytest -q tests/test_one_of_two_racing_reviews_survives.py` → 4 passed, EXIT=0) and the recorded negative control reddens both the race case and the ordering case (2 failed, 2 passed, exit 1); the two failures in the record's suite pair reproduce at base 2a0696ba with dispatch.py restored to its base revision (base-existing-conflicts.log, 2 failed/3 passed), and the added-failure count derived from the manifest's own baseline_suite/after_suite logs is 0 with no ids. Weakness: both arms of the recorded suite pair name only tests/test_dispatch_launch_is_not_its_own_conflict.py, narrower than the node's four-file gate, so the pair alone does not carry the new test file's passing arm — that arm is only in the manifest's tests field.
justifications.fit: the new symbols are mechanism-named (`_peer_claim_is_a_later_racing_arrival`, `_registered_at`, `launched`, `claim_registered_at`), the comments state the mechanism (why a still-composing claim is outranked, why a launched one is not), the test file's docstring states the race and the rule rather than a changelog, and no plan, phase, ticket or version label appears in the change.
justifications.goal_fidelity: every clause of the goal is present and correct in the diff: `_peer_claim_is_a_later_racing_arrival` returns True only for a peer that carries no worktree and no pid (`launched=False`) and whose (registered_at, run_id) sorts strictly after this dispatch's own, the helper is reached at both admission checks with this dispatch's own run id and registration timestamp, and the three terminal cases (launched peer, empty timestamp, dispatch holding no claim) all fall through to the pre-existing refusal — so exactly one of the two proceeds and the other refuses naming the registered-first run.
justifications.scope_discipline: `git diff --stat 2a0696ba544bdeb8fd66e0c2bdbf483488fa3e6d..4dc8ff94b3ac70d6f198e84e4262cd3a6b9e40c7` is exactly the three declared paths — reckon/crew/dispatch.py, tests/test_one_of_two_racing_reviews_survives.py and the evidence fragment — with no file outside them, and the reviewed worktree is clean at head with a single commit.
